VHistory - Get CDB Scalar History.vi

Owning Palette: Variabe History VIs

Returns the history of a variable that has the CDB Number data type. The specified variable must exist and have a history attached; otherwise, the VI returns an error. The VHistory - History Controller.vi is used to configure VarMan to maintain the history of a variable.
See the Variable history topic for more information.

Click the parameters for more information

 

VC Handle specifies the handle of the Variable Context in which the target variable exists. To operate on a global variable, pass -1 to this input or keep it unwired. VC Handle is ignored if name_spec refers to the variable by an alias. See the Referring to variables topic for more information.
name_spec defines the name specifier of the target variable. Usually, this is merely a variable name; however, additional options are available. See the Referring to variables topic for details.
N vals (all) is used only if the mode control is equal to N-Vals (1); otherwise, it is ignored. N vals specifies the desired number of newest history values to be returned. If N vals is greater than or equal to zero, and less than the actual number of values stored in the history, the VI returns N vals last values stored in the history. Otherwise, VI returns all history values. By default, N vals is equal to -1; i.e. VI returns the entire history.
time range (all) cluster is used only if the mode control is equal to TimeRange (0); otherwise, it is ignored. If both the t1 and t2 members of the cluster are equal to zero (default), the VI returns the entire history of the specified variable. Otherwise, the VI returns only values whose time stamps fall within the range from MIN(t1,t2) up to MAX(t1,t2).
t1 defines the first boundary of a time range.
t2 defines the second boundary of a time range.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
mode specifies the behavior of the VI. There are the following modes:

0TimeRangeVI returns history values that have time stamps in the range specified in time range cluster. It's default value.
1N-ValsVI returns as many newest history values as specified in N vals control, or entire history if number of stored values is less than N Vals.
2NewValsVI returns only values stored to the history after it was successfully read in NewVals mode last time. If no values have been added to the history after the last such reading, VI returns no values (empty history subset).
reverse order (T). If it equals TRUE (default), the VI returns values arranged in reverse chronological order (decreasing time stamps). If it equals FALSE, the VI returns values arranged in direct chronological order (increasing time stamps).
writer IDs is an array containing the Writer IDs for the respective elements in the history indicator, signaling the source of those historic values. This array is empty if the variable history does not maintain Writer IDs.
dup name_spec is a flow-through parameter with the same value as name_spec.
time stamps is an array of the time stamps (DBL representation), in the universal LabVIEW date/time format, for the respective elements in the history indicator.  Elements in the time stamps, history, and writer IDs arrays are arranged in the order specified by the reverse order control.
history is an array containing the historic variable values.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains VarMan VI error code identifying an error if any occurred. If no error occurred, it is equal to zero.
source contains the error description and VI location information if an error occurred.
